newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador paralyzed by 48-hour general strike.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador paralyzed by 48-hour general strike.

text.p: Ecuadorean industry and commerce was paralyzed Wednesday as unions began a 48-hour general strike to protest at government austerity measures and to call for the resignation of President Abdala Bucaram.
Banks, financial markets and industry in the capital Quito were closed and the government declared a "state of mobilization", allowing it to use troops to maintain order.
While Quito streets were quiet in the morning, unions planned a massive demonstration culminating in a march on Congress to demand Bucaram's resignation in the afternoon.
Government offices were also shut, as Bucaram had earlier given public workers a day off to coincide with the strike.
There was no confirmation that Ecuador's oil industry had stopped working, but oil industry unions earlier said that they would join the strike.

"To maintain the public order of the republic, (Bucaram) decreed the national mobilization of the human resources and materials needed to maintain order," said the President's spokesman Fernando Artieda.
Vice-President Rosalia Arteaga added to the turmoil surrounding the Ecuadorean government, declaring that she wants to replace Bucaram if he resigns or is dismissed from his post.
"Rosalia Arteaga is the constitutional option for the country, if we want to maintain democracy and stay within the bounds of the constitution," Arteaga said on local television.

In an address to the nation broadcast Tuesday night, Bucaram called for talks between the government, unions, social organizations, indigenous groups and business to "construct a new state" and stimulate the economy.

Opposition groups and students have staged waves of protests since the beginning of January when the six-month old government launched an economic austerity package, including price-hikes for electricity, telephones and public transport.
Bucaram said he respected the protests but he underlined that the government will not permit attacks on private property nor aggressive provocation.
On Tuesday a million Ecuadorean Indians started a major protest by blocking major roads across the country.
Truck drivers began an indefinite strike on Monday which has caused gasoline shortages throughout the country.
